greek.forms: First declension feminine. Singular: ἡδονή, ἡδονῆς, ἡδονῇ, ἡδονήν. Plural: ἡδοναί, ἡδονῶν, ἡδοναῖς, ἡδονάς.
greek.etymology: From ἡδύς (hay-DEES) 'sweet'. The root ἡδ- (HAYD) connects sweetness with enjoyment across Indo-European languages. English descendants: Hedonism (pursuit of pleasure), Hedonistic (pleasure-seeking), Hedonic (relating to pleasure), Anhedonia (inability to feel pleasure).
greek.usage_example: τὴν ἡδονὴν ἀγαθὸν εἶναι φαίνεται — Pleasure appears to be good
greek.did_you_know: Ancient Greeks distinguished between κίνησις (KEE-nay-sis) 'kinetic pleasure' (active enjoyment like sex or food) and κατάστημα (kah-TAHS-tay-mah) 'katastematic pleasure' (static contentment like peace of mind). Epicurus argued that katastematic pleasures were superior because they lasted longer and didn't lead to pain.
